result.title: GEM-MM: Reducing VLM Hallucination with Entropy-Guided Preference Alignment
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are routinely aligned with offline pairwise RLHF objectives, but multimodal preference data is scarce and treats every response token as equally informative. Under a small preference budget, pair construction becomes nearly irrelevant: standard DPO-style, image-conditional, and self-improvement objectives all perform within 1.1 points on MM-RLHF metrics and 0.5 points on hallucination rates, matching the SFT baseline. We call this entropy-blind preference optimization: the learning signal ignores policy uncertainty, which in chain-of-thought VLMs concentrates on specific fork tokens where visual claims are made. We introduce GEM-MM, extending entropy-guided preference modeling to VLMs. It samples on-policy candidates, rewards high-entropy reasoning forks, penalizes uncertain final answers, and updates the model via group-normalized policy gradients. On a 3000-prompt MM-RLHF budget with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, GEM-MM achieves the best entropy-depth preference score (61.7% vs. 57.3-58.4% baselines) and implicit-reward accuracy (41.4%). Crucially, it reduces AMBER hallucination from 23.4-24.0 to 20.6 and CHAIR from 5.0-5.1 to 4.6 at matched caption coverage. It also ranks best on all three HallusionBench granularities, with a conservative operating point raising the near-chosen rate to 62.4%. An off-the-shelf multimodal reward model ranks GEM-MM first, and two such models independently confirm our main ablations (p < 0.001). We report confidence intervals, paired significance tests, metric-reward functional overlaps, and document a collapse mode when exceeding the fair budget. Code and evaluation harness: https://github.com/SNOWTEAM2023/GEM-MM

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出多模态偏好预算有限时 DPO 类目标对策略不确定性「熵盲」，提出 GEM-MM：采样 on-policy 候选，奖励高熵推理分叉、惩罚不确定终答，并以组归一化策略梯度更新，在 MM-RLHF 预算下降低 AMBER、CHAIR 幻觉。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应推理轨迹的贡献分配与视觉证据使用：高熵分叉 token 正是视觉主张出现处，可供核查「THINK 是否有益」及幻觉成因，但其作用在显式 token 轨迹而非 latent 状态生成。
